page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It delivers 48 physical cores across 48 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 192.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in single-core and multi-core CPU metrics, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2396.0 and multi-core score of 28199.0. It delivers top-tier throughput in compilation tasks (93107.0 in Clang tests), data compression (36.5 GB/sec in gzip, 635.79 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression), and static web serving (104.04 GB/sec). Database performance is elevated, reaching 46541.54 in PassMark database operations and 136.39 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 6318.61 GB/sec, while uncached reads and writes perform within median ranges at 187.71 GB/sec and 85.27 GB/sec respectively.

Architecturally, the ARMv9 platform relies on standard AES cryptographic acceleration without x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX. Large language model inference yields mixed results: prompt processing performs strongly on smaller architectures (4218.03 tokens/sec on a 135M model), whereas token generation remains constrained, registering at 31.56 tokens/sec on 135M and 26.75 tokens/sec on 7B models. The combination of dense physical core allocation and high-speed local NVMe SSDs makes it efficient for I/O-heavy environments, though vector-heavy machine learning token generation is limited by the lack of dedicated accelerators.

The instance is best fitted for high-throughput transactional and in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, software compilation pipelines, large-scale web serving fleets, and data preprocessing tasks requiring substantial local NVMe storage and balanced memory-to-core ratios.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance powered by 48 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores running at 3.3 GHz. Configured with 192.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 25 Gbps network bandwidth, it lacks integrated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier performance in multi-core compilation (Geekbench Clang score of 93107.0), data decompression, static web serving throughput (104.04 GB/sec), and in-memory key-value processing, logging 136.39 million Redis SET operations per second. While uncached memory throughput and LLM token generation speeds fall into average or lower bands, its 48 dedicated physical cores and integrated local NVMe storage provide high efficiency for database systems, build servers, continuous integration workflows, and high-volume web applications.
